Tom Clinton also showed a return to his old form in being fifth, and although Ted Stimpson had a damaged leg he ran well to finish 17th. With Dick Tobin 36, J.
Ron Minahan, Eric Herbert, George Chantler, and Mike Heard also ran well, and an interesting entrant was Colin Sutton, the well-known walker. The handicap was won by J.

On the 8th May our lads went to Chichester for the 16 miles road race to Portsmouth and Dick Tobin was our first runner in 8th place, Bert Footer 9th, Bert Smith 10, George Chantler 14, Con Abberton 15, J.

… eventually Mike Heard was 11th with Jack Brown 13th and George Durrant 14th, which was a very good show on their part. J. McDonald was our sixth man in 28th position and Len Adams 38th and Lou Bush 40th gave good support.…
This event, which always opens our Winter programme, was held from Belgrave Hall on October 2nd, and a record field of 61 turned out. Arthur Bruce proved the winner of a good race with J.

When the handicap had been worked out it was found that J. McDonald was the winner and he certainly ran well in his usual determined style and there was a dead heat for second place between Jack Brown and "Ginger" Charlton, which the latter won on the toss of a coin with Brown taking third prize.

Dick Tobin, a member of our winning "National" team in 1946, is also showing signs of his old-time form, and we wish that Frank Abberton and Dick Towndrow could also strike their form of a few seasons ago in order to make up for the loss of our track "stars," who have decided not to do any serious r…
Mick Porter was also first home in 24th position in the Finchley 20 miles with Arthur Whitehead 39, Tom Carter 40, J. McDonald 41, Dick Towndrow 54 and Arthur Penstone 62nd.
Placings and times of our men were:—25, C. Abberton, 2.54.56; 28, J.
Also on the programme was a 15 miles road race and our lads finished 2nd to Mitcham A.C. in the team race and J. McDonald ran really well to finish 7th in a good class field.
Our first man to finish was J. McDonald, our Club Marathon Champion, in 16th position closely followed in by A.
Briggs second and J. McDonald third, and the latter must have found it a change from the usual long-distance runs which he has been indulging in.

Bob Taylor ran well to come home together with Glancy of Ealing in first place, and our next were Ken Stimpson 7th, J. McDonald 8th, and Dick Tobin 9th, and it was this trio who were mainly responsible for our winning the match by the narrow margin of ½ point.

Plummer, who finished 13th, but he is not yet qualified to represent us in open team races. This made J. McDonald, who was 26th, winning the award for first Club man home, and he was closely followed by Lou Bush and Frank Mitchell.
We thus finished 2nd in the team race to Herne Hill. Our other runner to finish was J.
Bishop, G.Pearson and J. McDonald who all ran well enough to give us second team place to Walton A.C.
On 24th September three of our distance runners, W. Wortley, A, Bishop and J. McDonald, just sufficient for a team, set off on the long run to Brighton.
